result.title: Google — Manage your service areas for service-area and hybrid businesses
result.description: Address-visibility, service-area limits, and definitions for SABs vs hybrid Business Profiles.
result.body:
Google's Business Profile Help page on service-area configuration. Used as the primary source in [GBP Verification](/gbp/verification.md) and [Business Type Detection](/local-seo/business-type-detection.md).

# What the source establishes

* Service-area businesses (visit/deliver to customers, no storefront — cleaners, plumbers) must remove their address; hybrid businesses (storefront plus delivery/visits, e.g. a restaurant with delivery) keep the address and add service areas.
* Up to 20 service areas, each defined by city, postal code, or similar geographic designation — never as a radius — and Google recommends staying within roughly a two-hour drive of the business's base location.

cases.response:
I’ll find and open the relevant saved knowledge page using the rim_openai_review tools.
I opened Rank-in-Maps’ [service-area address guidance](https://github.com/MrBigleg/okf-local-seo/blob/9b0d9883a05ca1bd80bb5e34df93ee2d9641b7fb/bundles/local-seo/references/google-gbp-service-areas.md).

- **Service-area business:** If it visits or delivers to customers and has no storefront, remove the address from its Google Business Profile.
- **Hybrid business:** If it has a storefront plus delivery or customer visits, keep the address and add service areas.
- Service areas use cities, postal codes or similar geographic designations—not a radius. The page states a maximum of 20 areas and recommends staying within roughly a two-hour drive of the base.

The page attributes this to [Google Business Profile Help](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481). **Limitations:** I read RIM’s pinned snapshot, dated July 27, 2026, rather than the live Google page. This explains the general rule; it does not establish whether Synthetic Reviewer Cafe A is a storefront, service-area or hybrid business.
